en: Full of quiet hints that point to other things
hook: ALLUSIVE: full of ALLUSIONS (hints), not to be confused with elusive (hard to catch).
story: Allusive. In Ishita's literature class, the teacher read a poem about 'a river that remembers nineteen seventy-one' and 'a rebel who wrote in fire.' No names were given, yet every Bangladeshi student understood the hints. The poem was allusive: full of indirect references to things outside it. Do not confuse allusive with elusive, which means hard to catch, or illusive, which means deceptive. An allusion is a hint, and allusive writing is full of them. Synonyms: suggestive, referential.

gre.s: Her poems are deeply ____, packed with veiled references to Persian mystics and Bengali folk songs that most readers miss on a first reading.
gre.clue: packed with veiled references

example: The cartoonist's allusive drawings rewarded readers who knew the week's headlines, since every figure hinted at a real minister.

en: Honest and natural, with no tricks or pretense
hook: ART-LESS: no art of trickery. Natural and honest.
story: Artless. At the dinner party, Auntie served her new chicken recipe and asked everyone what they thought. The adults said, "Delicious!" Then little Joya, aged six, announced, "It is too salty, but the dessert is very nice." Everyone laughed, including Auntie. Joya was not being rude. She simply had no tricks, no pretence, no social games. That is artless: natural, simple, and sincere, without deceit. It is a compliment. Artless means without the art of cunning, not without skill.

gre.s: The child's ____ remarks, free of any calculation or flattery, charmed the guests far more than the polished speeches of the adults.
gre.clue: free of any calculation or flattery

example: Moni's artless letter to the company, written in plain words without any flattery, persuaded the director to fund her school.

en: Harsh, loud, and unpleasant-sounding
hook: CACO = bad, PHONE = sound. Bad sound.
story: Cacophonous. At five in the evening, Gulistan intersection becomes a symphony from hell. Bus horns blare. Rickshaw bells jangle. A loudspeaker blasts film songs from one shop while another blasts a sermon. Vendors scream prices. A traffic policeman blows his whistle at no one in particular. Imran covered his ears and laughed. The noise was cacophonous: harsh, jarring, and unpleasant. Caco means bad, phone means sound. Its opposite is euphonious, meaning sweet to hear.

gre.s: The composer deliberately made the opening ____, layering clashing rhythms and harsh brass so that the gentle melody that follows seems all the sweeter.
gre.clue: layering clashing rhythms and harsh brass

example: Rush hour at Farmgate is cacophonous, a blare of bus horns, shouting conductors and revving motorbike engines.

en: A lie told on purpose to ruin someone's good name
hook: CALUMNY sounds like 'CALL YOU MONEY-thief', a lie that ruins your name.
story: Calumny. Two weeks before the election, anonymous posts flooded social media. They claimed that Ishita, the popular candidate, had stolen money meant for flood victims. Not a single word was true. There were no documents, no witnesses, only rumours designed to destroy her. Investigators later proved her innocence, but by then thousands of votes were lost. That was calumny: a false and malicious statement made to damage someone's reputation. Synonyms include slander and defamation.

gre.s: The memoir was less a balanced history than an act of ____, attributing invented crimes to the author's former rivals.
gre.clue: attributing invented crimes

example: Anonymous accounts spread calumny about the young journalist, claiming she had been paid by foreign spies.

en: Resting on guesses rather than solid proof
hook: CONJECTURE = a guess. CONJECTURAL = guess-based.
story: Conjectural. Professor Haque held up a broken clay pot. "This belonged to a king who ruled here two thousand years ago," he said. "I believe he died in battle." A student asked how he knew. He smiled. "I do not know. No written records survive. My account is conjectural, pieced together from coins, pots, and guesswork." Conjectural means based on guesswork or incomplete evidence. A conjecture is a guess. GRE passages contrast conjectural theories with empirical proof.

gre.s: Because no fossils from the period have been found, any account of the species' behavior must remain largely ____.
gre.clue: no fossils from the period have been found

example: Since the ancient city left no written records, our picture of its government is mostly conjectural.

en: To move or act slowly and waste time
hook: DAWDLE: like a DOODLE, wasting time drawing nothing.
story: Dawdle. Babu was sent to the bazaar to buy fish for lunch. On the way he stopped to watch a cricket match, chatted with the tea seller, and spent twenty minutes admiring a new motorbike. He came home at two o'clock, and his mother had already cooked dal and rice without him. "Stop dawdling," she said. To dawdle is to waste time or move slowly. Students dawdle before starting homework. Synonyms: dally, linger, loiter. Opposite: hasten.

gre.s: With the deadline only hours away, the team could not afford to ____; every minute spent idling would make the final report weaker.
gre.clue: every minute spent idling

example: The children dawdled on the way home from school, stopping at every stall that sold pickles and ice lollies.

en: Rigidly applying a theory without regard for practical considerations
hook: DOCTRINAIRE: follows the DOCTRINE no matter what.
story: Doctrinaire. A new manager at a garment factory near Dhaka had read one textbook on efficiency and believed every word. When workers explained that his new shift schedule ignored the monsoon flooding on their roads, he refused to change a single line, because the theory said so. Production collapsed. His approach was doctrinaire: rigidly applying a theory without regard for practical reality. The word comes from doctrine, a fixed set of beliefs. Opposite: pragmatic. Synonyms: dogmatic, inflexible.

gre.s: Unlike her ____ predecessor, who insisted on following party ideology even when it produced obvious failures, the new minister was willing to adapt policies to local conditions.
gre.clue: insisted on following party ideology even when it produced obvious failures

example: The doctrinaire economist insisted that markets would fix everything, even as prices of rice and lentils doubled.

en: To teach someone in a way that improves their mind or character
hook: EDIFY: builds you up like an EDIFICE (building).
story: Edify. Every evening during load-shedding, Grandfather lit a lantern and told the children stories. A greedy king who lost everything. A poor boy who returned a lost wallet. A girl who studied by candlelight and became a doctor. The stories entertained them, but they also quietly taught honesty, patience, and courage. Grandfather meant to edify: to improve someone morally or intellectually. An edifying documentary teaches you something valuable. Edify shares a root with edifice: it builds you up.

gre.s: The museum's new exhibits are designed to ____ as well as entertain, teaching visitors about climate science through interactive games.
gre.clue: teaching visitors about climate science

example: Her grandfather's long evening stories were meant to edify as much as amuse, each one ending with a lesson about honesty.

en: Shameless boldness; insolent nerve
hook: EFFRONTERY: right in your FRONT, shamelessly.
story: Effrontery. A student was caught copying answers from his phone during an exam. When the invigilator confiscated the phone, the student demanded it back and insisted that the invigilator apologise for disturbing his concentration. The whole hall gasped at his effrontery: shameless boldness, insolent nerve. The word comes from the Latin effrons, barefaced, from frons, the forehead: someone with a brazen face who cannot blush. Compare temerity, which is rash boldness. Synonyms: impudence, gall, audacity.

gre.s: Caught plagiarizing an entire chapter, the author had the ____ to accuse his critics of jealousy, as though they rather than he were at fault.
gre.clue: as though they rather than he were at fault

example: The contractor who built the crumbling bridge had the effrontery to bid for the job of repairing it.

en: Possible to account for with a reason
hook: EXPLICABLE: can be EXPLAINED.
story: Explicable. Rafi's practice scores suddenly dropped from 315 to 298. His friends were puzzled. Was it bad luck? Was the test harder? Then his roommate mentioned that Rafi had been studying until four every morning and sleeping three hours a night. Suddenly the mystery was entirely explicable: able to be explained. Explicable is the opposite of the more familiar word inexplicable, meaning impossible to explain. Once you see the cause, a mystery becomes explicable.

gre.s: What at first seemed a baffling drop in sales became perfectly ____ once analysts noticed that a rival had launched a cheaper product that month.
gre.clue: once analysts noticed

example: The strange lights over the village became explicable once someone found the drone hobbyist living by the river.

en: Very fertile; capable of producing abundantly; intellectually productive
hook: FECUND: FERTILE and fruitful; produces a FECUND harvest.
story: Fecund. Every monsoon, the great rivers of Bangladesh flood their banks and leave behind a thick layer of fresh silt. When the water recedes, farmers plant immediately, and the land produces three rice harvests a year. The delta is one of the most fecund regions on Earth: extremely fertile and productive. Fecund is also used for minds. A fecund imagination produces endless creative ideas. Think: fertile and fruitful.

gre.s: The novelist's ____ imagination produced more than forty books in two decades, each populated by dozens of memorable characters.
gre.clue: produced more than forty books in two decades

example: The delta's fecund silt allows farmers in Bangladesh to grow three crops of rice on the same field each year.

en: To refrain from doing something; to hold back
hook: FOR-BEAR: BEAR (endure) it FOR now, and hold yourself back.
story: Forbear. At the Eid dinner, Sara's aunt said loudly, "Still not married? And so thin!" Sara felt the words rising in her throat. She wanted to tell her aunt exactly what she thought. Instead, she took a slow breath, smiled, and passed the rice. She forbore, for the sake of family peace. To forbear is to hold yourself back from doing or saying something. Do not confuse it with forebear, which means an ancestor.

gre.s: Though provoked repeatedly by the hecklers, the speaker managed to ____ from responding and simply continued his talk.
gre.clue: simply continued his talk

example: Doctors urged my diabetic grandfather to forbear eating sweets, yet every Eid he quietly helped himself to a bowl of shemai.

en: A messy, tangled situation that is hard to escape
hook: IMBROGLIO: an EMBROIDERY of tangled threads.
story: Imbroglio. It began with a forwarded message in a family group chat. One cousin misread it as an insult, an aunt took sides, two uncles stopped speaking, a wedding invitation was withdrawn, and somehow an old land dispute was revived. Nobody remembered the original message. It was an imbroglio: an extremely confused, complicated or embarrassing situation. The word is Italian, related to embroil, to tangle someone up. Synonyms: entanglement, muddle, mess.

gre.s: What began as a minor accounting error grew into a diplomatic ____ involving three governments, two banks, and a tangle of contradictory lawsuits.
gre.clue: a tangle of contradictory lawsuits

example: A double-booked wedding hall in Uttara led to an imbroglio involving two families, three caterers and the local police.

en: Free from injury or violation; untouched
hook: IN-VIOLATE: NOT VIOLATED.
story: Inviolate. In one village near Sylhet, there is a small forest beside an old shrine. For generations, nobody has cut a single tree there, hunted a bird, or even carried away fallen branches. The villagers believe the grove is sacred. It has remained inviolate: free from injury or violation, completely untouched. In means not, so inviolate means not violated. A promise or a principle can also be inviolate. Synonyms: untouched, intact, sacrosanct.

gre.s: For centuries the sacred grove remained ____: villagers believed that anyone who cut even a single branch would bring disaster on the whole community.
gre.clue: anyone who cut even a single branch would bring disaster

example: The scholar kept her promise of confidentiality inviolate, refusing to name her sources even when a court demanded it.

en: Completely clear and transparent; easy to understand
hook: LIMPID: clear as a LIMPID pool where you can see the bottom.
story: Limpid. At Bichanakandi, a stream flows down from the hills of Meghalaya so clear that Sara could see every pebble on its bed, every tiny fish darting between the stones, even a ring someone had dropped long ago. Later, her guide explained the region's history in a few simple, beautiful sentences that anyone could follow. Both the water and his words were limpid: completely clear and transparent. Synonyms: lucid, pellucid.

gre.s: Unlike his convoluted early essays, the philosopher's later works are written in ____ prose that even beginners can follow.
gre.clue: that even beginners can follow

example: Divers in the limpid waters around Saint Martin's Island can watch coral and fish several meters below the surface.

en: Looking or sounding sad and dismal
hook: LUGUBRIOUS: LUG-ubrious, LUGGING sadness around.
story: Lugubrious. Tanvir's old neighbour plays sad songs on his harmonium every evening. His face is long, his voice is slow and heavy, and even his jokes sound like funeral speeches. When he says good morning, it sounds like bad news. He is lugubrious: looking or sounding sad and dismal, often in an exaggerated way. The word comes from the Latin lugere, to mourn. Notice the long, slow, heavy sound of the word itself. Synonyms: mournful, doleful, gloomy.

gre.s: The director's films are relentlessly ____: long, slow scenes of grieving widows set to funeral music leave audiences longing for even a moment of levity.
gre.clue: long, slow scenes of grieving widows set to funeral music

example: The lugubrious face of the bloodhound made the children feel sorry for it, though it was perfectly content.

en: Sentimental in an exaggerated or false way
hook: MAWKISH: makes you want to say 'mock-ish', sickly sweet.
story: Mawkish. The TV drama's final episode lasted three hours. Every scene had slow-motion tears, violins swelling dramatically, characters declaring their feelings in long speeches, and a puppy appearing at sad moments. Viewers who began crying soon began rolling their eyes instead. It was mawkish: sentimental in an exaggerated, false, sickly way. A mawkish greeting card is so sugary it makes you wince. It tries too hard to make you feel.

gre.s: The critic praised the film for treating its tragic subject with restraint, avoiding the ____ excesses of earlier versions that had wallowed in tearful melodrama.
gre.clue: wallowed in tearful melodrama

example: The wedding video was spoiled by mawkish background music that swelled whenever anyone so much as smiled.

en: To calm someone's anger or anxiety
hook: MOLLIFY: make MOLLY soft and calm again.
story: Mollify. Priya forgot her best friend's birthday. Joya was hurt and stopped answering her messages. So Priya cooked Joya's favourite payesh, wrote a long handwritten apology, and turned up at her door with a small gift. Slowly Joya smiled. Priya had mollified her: she had calmed her anger. Moll comes from a Latin word meaning soft: to mollify is to soften someone's feelings. Synonyms: placate, appease, pacify. Its opposite is to provoke or enrage.

gre.s: Hoping to ____ the furious passengers, the airline manager promised full refunds and apologized personally to each traveller.
gre.clue: promised full refunds and apologized personally

example: The landlord mollified the angry tenants by lowering the rent for the months their water supply had failed.

en: Having a strong spiritual or mysterious quality
hook: NUMINOUS: sounds like LUMINOUS, glowing with something divine.
story: Numinous. Early one morning, Mitu entered an ancient Buddhist temple in Rangamati. Incense smoke curled through shafts of golden light. A monk chanted softly somewhere unseen, and a single bell rang. She stopped walking. Something about the stillness felt sacred, mysterious, larger than her. She felt the numinous: a strong spiritual or mysterious quality, suggesting a divine presence. Some people feel the numinous in nature too, beneath a sky full of stars.

gre.s: Visitors describe the ancient forest as almost ____, a place whose silence and towering trees seem to suggest a divine presence.
gre.clue: seem to suggest a divine presence

example: Standing alone in the vast cathedral at dawn, the tourist felt a numinous hush that she could not explain.

en: Stubbornly refusing to change one's opinion or action
hook: OB-DURATE: DURABLE stubbornness, hardened.
story: Obdurate. For six months, villagers begged the factory owner to stop dumping waste into their river. Scientists showed him test results. Fishermen showed him dead fish. Even the local imam asked him to reconsider. He would not budge an inch. He was obdurate: stubbornly refusing to change his opinion or his actions. The word shares a root with durable, from the Latin for hard; an obdurate person has a hardened heart. Synonyms: intransigent, inflexible, unyielding.

gre.s: Despite mounting evidence that his policy was failing, the minister remained ____, refusing even to consider the modest changes his own advisors proposed.
gre.clue: refusing even to consider the modest changes

example: My obdurate aunt would not leave her flooded house in Sirajganj until the water reached her kitchen shelves.

en: Deceitfulness; betrayal of trust
hook: PERFIDY: per-FID-y, breaking FIDelity (faithfulness).
story: Perfidy. In 1757, at the Battle of Plassey, Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah trusted his commander, Mir Jafar, to lead a large part of his army. Mir Jafar had secretly made a deal with the British. On the battlefield, his troops simply stood still. The Nawab lost, and Bengal fell under British control. Mir Jafar's perfidy is remembered to this day: deliberate betrayal of trust. In Bangladesh, his name itself means traitor.

gre.s: The spy's ____ came to light only after his death, when documents revealed that he had sold his country's secrets for decades.
gre.clue: sold his country's secrets for decades

example: Bengali schoolbooks still recall the perfidy of Mir Jafar, whose betrayal at Plassey helped the British win the battle.

en: Self-important, overly formal behavior or speech
hook: POMPOSITY: POMP and show of importance.
story: Pomposity. At the opening of a new community centre, the local official spoke for an hour. He used long, formal words where simple ones would do, reminded everyone of his many titles, and called himself 'this humble servant of the nation' while demanding the best chair. People laughed quietly behind their hands. His pomposity was hard to bear: self-important, overly formal behaviour and speech. Pomp means grand display, as in pomp and ceremony. Synonyms: self-importance, grandiosity, bombast.

gre.s: The ambassador's ____ was legendary: he insisted on being addressed by all three of his honorary titles and once refused to enter a hall through a side door.
gre.clue: insisted on being addressed by all three of his honorary titles

example: The new principal's pomposity amused the students, who mimicked his habit of quoting Latin at morning assembly.

en: One of the many results, often hidden, that follow a decision
hook: RAMIFICATION: branches (rami) spreading out from a decision.
story: Ramification. The government raised the price of diesel by twenty taka. It seemed a small change. But soon bus fares rose, then vegetable prices climbed because trucks cost more to run, and farmers could no longer afford to run their irrigation pumps. Each of these was a ramification: a complex, often unexpected consequence. Ramus is Latin for branch, so one decision branches out into many results. Synonyms: consequence, repercussion, implication.

gre.s: The committee hastily approved the plan without weighing a single ____ of its decision; within a year, unforeseen effects had rippled through every department.
gre.clue: unforeseen effects had rippled through every department

example: Few voters grasped the ramifications of the trade deal until local jute mills began closing one after another.

en: Calm and showing little emotion; dull
hook: STOLID: SOLID as a stone, no emotion shows.
story: Stolid. When the cyclone warning siren wailed over the coastal village, everyone rushed about in panic, except old Karim chacha. He slowly finished his tea, folded his newspaper, and walked to the shelter at his usual pace, his face showing nothing at all. His neighbors called him stolid: calm, impassive, showing little emotion. It can be praise, meaning steady and dependable, or criticism, meaning dull and unimaginative. A stolid person is as unmoved as a solid rock. Synonyms: impassive, phlegmatic.

gre.s: Even when the verdict was announced and his family erupted in tears, the defendant remained ____, his face betraying no hint of relief or anguish.
gre.clue: his face betraying no hint of relief or anguish

example: The stolid ferry captain steered through the storm without a word while passengers clung to the railings in panic.

en: To include or absorb something into a larger category
hook: SUB-SUME: SUM it UNDER a larger heading.
story: Subsume. When the government merged three small banks into one large national bank, the old names disappeared from the signboards, and customers of all three became customers of the new bank. The small banks had been subsumed: included or absorbed into something larger. In the same way, mango is subsumed under the category of fruit. Sub means under, and sume means take, as in assume and consume: to subsume is to take something under a larger umbrella. Synonyms: absorb, incorporate, encompass.

gre.s: Some linguists think it misleading to ____ Chittagonian into the broader category of Bengali dialects, since speakers of the two can barely understand each other.
gre.clue: since speakers of the two can barely understand each other

example: After the merger, the small regional bank was subsumed under its partner's brand, and its old logo disappeared from every branch.

en: Promoting a particular point of view, especially a controversial one; biased
hook: TENDENTIOUS: has a TENDENCY to favor one side.
story: Tendentious. The documentary claimed to be neutral. But it interviewed only one side, played dramatic, sinister music whenever the other side appeared, and quietly left out facts that did not fit its argument. Viewers noticed. Critics called it tendentious: written or presented to promote a particular, often controversial, point of view; biased. Think: it has a tendency to lean one way. GRE passages sometimes describe a tendentious reading of history.

gre.s: The reviewer dismissed the study as ____, noting that its authors had selected only the evidence that supported their political agenda.
gre.clue: selected only the evidence that supported their political agenda

example: The textbook's tendentious account of the war praised one general endlessly and ignored the civilians who suffered.

en: Eager to argue or fight; aggressively defiant
hook: TRUCULENT: like a TRUCK driver ready to fight anyone in traffic.
story: Truculent. A bus driver scraped a car in Farmgate traffic. Instead of apologizing, he jumped out, shouting and waving his fists, ready to fight anyone who came near. The car's owner backed away. Passengers sighed; this happened every week with him. He was truculent: eager to argue or fight, aggressively defiant. Truculent is a close synonym of belligerent and pugnacious. Picture a truck driver ready to fight everyone on the road.

gre.s: The ____ witness refused to answer even routine questions, glaring at the prosecutor and threatening to walk out of the courtroom.
gre.clue: glaring at the prosecutor and threatening to walk out

example: Grounded for a week, the truculent teenager slammed doors and refused to speak to anyone at dinner.

en: Complete and unreserved; pure
hook: UN-ALLOYED: pure gold, not mixed into an ALLOY.
story: Unalloyed. When Mahin opened the email saying he had won a full scholarship to study abroad, he screamed, danced around the room, and called his mother, who burst into happy tears. There was no worry and no doubt mixed in, only joy. It was unalloyed delight: complete, unreserved and pure. An alloy is a metal mixed with another, like brass. So unalloyed means not mixed with anything, like pure gold. Synonyms: pure, unmitigated, sheer.

gre.s: Her joy at the verdict was hardly ____, for though her brother had been freed, the real culprit had escaped justice entirely.
gre.clue: though her brother had been freed, the real culprit had escaped justice

example: For the village, the news that its girls' team had reached the national final brought unalloyed delight.

en: A feeling of irritation or worry caused by something troubling
hook: VEXATION: VEXED, constantly bothered.
story: Vexation. Tanvir spent four hours completing his university application, carefully uploading every document. Three hours before the deadline, he clicked Submit. The page froze. The internet had died. The router lights blinked red. He nearly threw his laptop out of the window. To his great vexation, he had to run to a cyber café across the city. Vexation means the state of being annoyed, frustrated, or worried. A vexing problem is irritatingly hard to solve.

gre.s: Much to the ____ of the organizers, heavy rain forced them to cancel the outdoor concert just an hour before it was due to begin.
gre.clue: forced them to cancel the outdoor concert

example: To the vexation of the commuters, the metro rail stopped between stations for forty minutes without any announcement.

en: Speaking fluently, readily, and continuously
hook: VOLUBLE: speaks in VOLUMES.
story: Voluble. Shuvo's grandmother could talk for hours without pause. She would start with the price of fish, move on to a neighbor's wedding, recall a story from the Liberation War, and come back to fish, all without stopping for breath. Visitors could hardly squeeze in a word. She was voluble: speaking fluently, readily, and continuously. It comes from the Latin volvere, to roll, as words roll out of the mouth. Its opposite is taciturn. Synonyms: talkative, loquacious, garrulous.

gre.s: Usually ____ at dinner parties, chatting easily with strangers for hours, the novelist became oddly taciturn whenever anyone asked about her new book.
gre.clue: chatting easily with strangers for hours

example: The voluble street vendor kept up a steady stream of jokes and sales talk, never pausing to catch his breath.
